mainTopic: Why the ברייתא's list of ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike includes some shared rules and leaves out others.
overview: This amud opens in the middle of a ברייתא that lists ways a גט and a שטר שחרור follow the same rules. The last listed item is that documents from gentile courts are kosher, except for these two. רבי מאיר counts a fourth way: the sender may take back either one before it is delivered. The גמרא asks what רבי מאיר's number 'four' rules out. It answers that it rules out the stencil method for witnesses who cannot write, which רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows only for a גט. Next the גמרא asks why other shared rules are missing from the list. 'Not given after death' is left out because it applies to ordinary documents too, as רבי יוחנן's ruling about a dying man's gift shows. לשמה and מחובר are left out because the list covers only rules from the רבנן, not from the Torah. Then the גמרא asks why gentile-court documents are listed if they seem invalid by Torah law. It answers that this follows רבי אלעזר, for whom the handover witnesses make the גט work. The amud ends with a challenge from a משנה, which suggests the תנא קמא does not hold like רבי אלעזר. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Gentile-court documents, and רבי מאיר's fourth similarity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its list of three. Documents made in gentile courts are kosher, except for a גט and a שטר שחרור. רבי מאיר adds a fourth similarity: the sender may take back either one before it is delivered.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Documents] that come out of gentile courts are kosher, even though gentiles signed them. The exceptions are bills of divorce and bills of freeing slaves. According to רבי מאיר, they are alike in four ways. If a man says 'Give this גט to my wife, and this שטר שחרור to my slave,' and he wants to take back both, he may take them back. These are the words of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא states its third way that a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike: neither one may be made in a gentile court. Then רבי מאיר adds a fourth way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most documents from a gentile court are kosher, but a גט and a שטר שחרור are not, so here the two are alike. רבי מאיר says they are also alike in another way: before delivery, the sender can cancel either one. This fourth item is רבי מאיר's own view. The רבנן do not count it, which is why the ברייתא's main count is only three.

keyTerms.meaning: Gentile courts or record offices where documents are drawn up
Their signers (the witnesses who sign)
Bills of divorce for wives
Documents that free slaves
To take back / cancel

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי מאיר is arguing about the gentile-court rule. He agrees with all three items and simply adds a fourth one.

phrases.english: [Documents] that come out of gentile courts,
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of the ברייתא. The word 'documents' was said just before, so the text here leaves it out.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁחוֹתְמֵיהֶן גּוֹיִם – כְּשֵׁירִין,
phrases.english: even though their signers are gentiles, are kosher,
except for bills of divorce and bills freeing slaves.
And according to רבי מאיר, [they are alike] in four [ways]:
one who says, 'Give this גט to my wife,
and this document of freedom to my slave,'
if he wants to take back both of them, he may take them back,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that was already in progress before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Documents from gentile courts are kosher, except a גט and a שטר שחרור. רבי מאיר adds that the sender may cancel either one before delivery.

steps.title: Why does רבי מאיר give a number?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why the רבנן say 'three': it leaves out רבי מאיר's extra item. But what does רבי מאיר's number 'four' leave out?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for the רבנן: their number leaves out רבי מאיר's item. But for רבי מאיר, what does the number come to leave out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what purpose רבי מאיר's count of 'four' serves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A number in a list usually means 'only this many.' The רבנן's 'three' clearly means 'not רבי מאיר's fourth.' רבי מאיר could have just said 'there is also another one.' By saying 'four,' he seems to be ruling out some fifth item, and we need to know what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for one side)
The number (the count given in the list)
To leave out / exclude

phrases.english: It makes sense according to the רבנן,
[that] the number [three] comes to leave out this item of רבי מאיר.
But according to רבי מאיר,
what does the number [four] come to leave out?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבָּנַן מִנְיָנָא לְמַעוֹטֵי הָא דְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר מִנְיָנָא לְמַעוֹטֵי מַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording 'four' in רבי מאיר's statement from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's use of the number 'four'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A number in a list is meant to rule something out. The רבנן's 'three' rules out רבי מאיר's item, but nothing obvious is ruled out by 'four.'

steps.title: The number leaves out the paper-stencil rule
steps.stepSummary: The 'four' leaves out a ברייתא about witnesses who cannot write. A stencil of their names is cut out of blank paper, and they fill in the gaps with ink.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to leave out what was taught in a ברייתא: for witnesses who do not know how to sign, we tear blank paper for them, and they fill in the torn spaces with ink.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by bringing a ברייתא about witnesses who cannot write their names. It is setting up the next step, which shows how this ruling relates to רבי מאיר's count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses who cannot write are given a paper stencil of their names, and they trace over it with ink. The next step will show this rule works differently for a גט and a שטר שחרור. That difference is what רבי מאיר's 'four' rules out.

keyTerms.meaning: That was taught in a ברייתא
We tear / cut out
Blank paper
Ink

phrases.english: To leave out this, which was taught in a ברייתא:
witnesses who do not know how to sign,
we tear blank paper for them,
phrases.notes: He means the shapes of their names are cut out of the paper, like a stencil laid on the document.

phrases.english: and they fill in the torn spaces with ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an outside ruling that the number comes to exclude.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי מאיר's 'four' seemed to have no purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: The number rules out the idea that the stencil rule applies equally to both documents.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the stencil rule to a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the stencil method applies only to a גט. For a שטר שחרור and all other documents, witnesses sign only if they can read and write.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said: When is this said? For bills of divorce. But for documents freeing slaves and all other documents, if the witnesses know how to read and sign, they sign; if not, they do not sign.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל saying the stencil method is allowed only for a גט. This completes the answer: on this rule a גט and a שטר שחרור are NOT alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר agrees with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל that here the two documents are different. So when he says 'four,' he means 'only four.' That excludes thinking that the תנא קמא's stencil rule makes a fifth similarity covering both documents.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case is this said? (a limiting phrase)
All other documents
To read and to sign

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן list three ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike, and רבי מאיר lists four. רבי מאיר's 'four' teaches that the stencil method for witnesses who cannot write is NOT one of the shared rules. It is allowed only for a גט, as רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says.
steps.confusionAlert: The stencil leniency is for a גט only. It does not apply to a שטר שחרור, even though the two documents are alike in the other listed ways.

phrases.english: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said:
In what case is this said? For bills of divorce,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שִׁחְרוּרֵי עֲבָדִים וּשְׁאָר כׇּל הַשְּׁטָרוֹת,
phrases.english: but documents freeing slaves and all other documents,
if [the witnesses] know how to read and sign, they sign,
and if not, they do not sign.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in step 3 and shows why it answers step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the two documents differ on this rule, so the count 'four' is meaningful.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the stencil rule applies to both a גט and a שטר שחרור, making a fifth similarity.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי מאיר holds like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the stencil method is for a גט only, so 'four' excludes a fifth similarity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic method of the גמרא: every number in a list is checked for what it comes to rule out.

steps.title: Who said anything about reading?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's wording. The earlier ברייתא only talked about witnesses who cannot write, so why does he mention reading?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל talks about witnesses who 'can read,' even though nobody before him mentioned reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא only dealt with witnesses who cannot sign their names. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל answers by saying witnesses sign only if they can 'read and write.' His mention of reading seems to be a reply to something that was never said.

keyTerms.meaning: Reading
Who mentioned it? (Said when someone answers a point nobody raised)

phrases.english: Reading — who mentioned it?
phrases.notes: He means: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל spoke about reading, but the opinion he was answering never brought it up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'can read and write' in רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's statement.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A reply should answer what was actually said. The first opinion never mentioned reading, so there was nothing about reading for him to answer.

steps.title: The ברייתא is missing a line about witnesses who cannot read
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is missing words. The full version says that if witnesses cannot read, someone reads the document to them and they sign. If they cannot write, the stencil is cut for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא is missing words, and this is what it means: witnesses who cannot read have the document read to them, and then they sign. Witnesses who cannot write have a stencil cut for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in a missing line in the ברייתא. Now the first opinion does mention reading, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's reply makes sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The added line gives the first opinion two easy rules: one for witnesses who cannot read, and one for witnesses who cannot write. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees about both, except in the case of a גט. That is why his reply mentions both reading and writing.

keyTerms.meaning: Words are missing, and this is what it teaches (the גמרא fills in a gap in the text)
Someone reads the document out loud in front of them
Paper is cut for them (the stencil of their names)

phrases.english: It is missing words, and this is what it teaches:
Witnesses who do not know how to read —
someone reads it in front of them, and they sign;
and those who do not know how to sign —
paper is cut for them.
phrases.notes: This is the stencil from step 3: their names are cut out of the paper and they fill in the gaps with ink.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by filling in a missing line.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Filling in missing words in the ברייתא (חסורי מחסרא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first opinion only spoke about witnesses who cannot write, so mentioning reading made no sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first opinion also allowed witnesses who cannot read to sign after the document is read to them. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is replying to both rules.

steps.title: Isn't there another way they are alike: not given after death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the list of ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike stops where it does. Another shared rule exists: if the sender dies, neither one is given. A gift of money, by contrast, is given even after the giver dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there nothing else? But there is this rule: someone who says 'Give this גט to my wife and this שטר שחרור to my slave' and then dies — they are not given after his death. If he says 'Give a מנה to so-and-so' and then dies, it is given after his death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list of shared rules by pointing to another rule that a גט and a שטר שחרור have in common.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט and a שטר שחרור both stop working once the sender dies, so they cannot be delivered afterward. A gift of money is still delivered after death. This seems to be another clear way the two documents are alike, so why didn't the ברייתא (or רבי מאיר, who counted four) list it?

keyTerms.meaning: And is there nothing more?
After death
A sum of money (one hundred דינרים)
So-and-so

phrases.english: And is there nothing more?!
But there is this: one who says,
'Give this גט to my wife,
and this שטר שחרור to my slave,' and he died —
they may not give them after his death;
'Give a מנה to so-and-so,' and he died —
they give it after his death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list of shared rules from steps 1–2 and asks why one more rule was left out.
steps.kashyaTarget: The count of shared rules (three or four) in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the list is meant to include the rules a גט and a שטר שחרור share, the rule that neither is given after death should also be on it.

steps.title: The list only includes rules that ordinary documents do not share
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא only lists rules that are special to a גט and a שטר שחרור. It leaves out rules that also apply to ordinary documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it teaches, it lists things that do not apply to ordinary documents. Things that do apply to ordinary documents it does not list.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the rule behind the list: it includes only what makes these two documents different from ordinary ones. This hints that 'not given after death' also applies to ordinary documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on a claim: the 'not after death' rule is not special to a גט and a שטר שחרור. The מנה case seemed different, but the גמרא will show that when an ordinary document is needed, it also cannot be made after death. That proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A rule that does not apply to ordinary documents
Ordinary legal documents (loans, sales, gifts)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the 'not after death' rule is false for a גט. It is true. It is left off the list only because it is not special to a גט and a שטר שחרור.

phrases.english: When it teaches, it teaches a matter that does not apply to ordinary documents;
a matter that does apply to ordinary documents, it does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 7 by explaining what kind of rule belongs on the list.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list includes every rule a גט and a שטר שחרור share.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list includes only shared rules that ordinary documents do not have. The 'not after death' rule applies to ordinary documents too, so it is left out.

steps.title: Proof: an ordinary gift document is also not written after death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its answer with a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל in the name of רבי יוחנן. If a dying man says 'Write and give a מנה to so-and-so' and then dies, they do not write and give it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבין sent in the name of רבי אבהו: You should know that רבי אלעזר sent to the Diaspora in the name of our teacher: a dying man who said 'Write and give a מנה to so-and-so,' and then died — they do not write and give it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that the 'not after death' rule also applies to ordinary documents. The reason for the ruling comes in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, a gift of money was given after death. That was a case where the man only said 'give.' Here he said 'write and give,' so a document is involved, and they do not write it after he dies. So the rule that a document is not made after death is not special to a גט and a שטר שחרור.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is very sick and may die (on his deathbed)
Write and give
You should know
The Diaspora (בבל)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that what matters is whether the man asked for a document. When he did, his death stops the document from being written, just like a גט.

phrases.english: As רבין sent in the name of רבי אבהו:

phrases.aramaic: הֱווּ יוֹדְעִין, שֶׁשָּׁלַח רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לַגּוֹלָה
phrases.english: You should know that רבי אלעזר sent to the Diaspora
in the name of our teacher:
A man on his deathbed who said,
'Write and give a מנה to so-and-so,' and he died —
they do not write and give it,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 8 that the 'not after death' rule also applies to ordinary documents.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the 'not after death' rule is not special to a גט and a שטר שחרור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling, sent by רבי אלעזר and reported by רבין in the name of רבי אבהו: if a dying man says 'write and give' and then dies, the document is not written.

steps.title: Why the dying man's gift is not written after his death
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's ruling. The dying man may have wanted to give the money only through a שטר, and a שטר cannot be written after the giver dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe he decided to give it to him only through a document, and a document cannot be written after death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why, in רבי יוחנן's case from Step 9, the document is not written after the man dies. This finishes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man said 'write and give,' so maybe he wanted the gift to happen only through a שטר. A שטר made after the owner's death cannot transfer anything. So the rule 'not after death' applies to ordinary documents too, which is why the ברייתא did not list it as special to a גט and a שטר שחרור.

keyTerms.meaning: decided firmly, made up his mind
to transfer ownership to him
after death

steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the support for the answer in Step 8: the ברייתא lists only rules that are special to a גט and a שטר שחרור.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר,
phrases.english: Perhaps he decided to transfer it to him only with a document,
and there is no document after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁמָּא לֹא גָּמַר לְהַקְנוֹתוֹ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁטָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's ruling quoted in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'not given after death' also applies to ordinary documents, so it is not special to a גט and a שטר שחרור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן's ruling about the dying man's מנה, explained as: a שטר cannot be written after death.

steps.title: What about the rule of writing it for her sake?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the list again: both a גט and a שטר שחרור must be written לשמה, so why is that not listed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the rule of 'for her sake'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out another rule that a גט and a שטר שחרור share, which the ברייתא did not list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both documents must be written specifically for the woman or the slave who receives them. This seems to be a rule special to these two documents, so by the standard of Step 8 it should have been on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: for her sake: written specifically for the person receiving it
but there is (introduces a missing item)

phrases.english: But isn't there the rule of 'for her sake'?
phrases.notes: Both documents must be written for the specific woman or slave receiving them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the omission of 'not after death,' the גמרא raises a new missing item.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the ברייתא's list of ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: לשמה is shared by both documents and does not apply to ordinary documents, so by the rule in Step 8 it should be listed.

steps.title: It works for רבה but not for רבא
steps.stepSummary: According to רבה, לשמה is already included in the listed rule of 'delivering and bringing.' According to רבא, the question still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is fine according to רבה: this is the 'delivering and bringing' rule. But according to רבא, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a partial answer. It works for רבה, but for רבא the difficulty still stands for now. Step 14 resolves it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה holds that the messenger says 'it was written in my presence' to confirm it was written לשמה. For him, the listed rule of 'delivering and bringing' already covers לשמה. רבא holds that the statement is needed to confirm the document's signatures, so for him לשמה is still missing from the list.

keyTerms.meaning: it is understandable / granted
delivering and bringing: the rule that a messenger bringing the document must make a declaration
it is difficult

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רַבָּה and רָבָא. They are two different אמוראים with different reasons for the messenger's declaration.

phrases.english: Granted according to Rabba, this is 'delivering and bringing.'
phrases.notes: For רבה, the messenger's declaration exists because of לשמה, so that listed rule already covers it.

phrases.english: But according to Rava, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: For רבא, the declaration is about confirming the signatures, so לשמה is not covered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11 for רבה only, and sharpens it against רבא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Partial answer: the item is already included in another listed rule, but only according to one view.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לשמה is missing from the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבה it is included under 'delivering and bringing.' According to רבא the problem remains.

steps.title: What about a document written on something attached to the ground?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another question that works against both רבה and רבא: a document written while attached to the ground is invalid for both a גט and a שטר שחרור, yet it is not listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: both according to רבה and according to רבא, there is the rule of 'attached'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second missing item. Even רבה's approach cannot explain this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט or שטר שחרור written on something still attached to the ground, like a leaf on a tree, is invalid. The 'delivering and bringing' rule does not cover this for anyone, so the question works against both views.

keyTerms.meaning: and furthermore
attached to the ground

phrases.english: And furthermore: both according to Rabba and according to Rava,
there is the rule of 'attached'!
phrases.notes: He means a document written on something still growing, like a leaf on a tree.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: בֵּין לְרַבָּה בֵּין לְרָבָא, הָאִיכָּא מְחוּבָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second missing item that works against both views, making the question stronger.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the ברייתא's list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule of מחובר applies to both documents and is not explained by the 'delivering and bringing' rule under either view.

steps.title: The list covers only rabbinic rules
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists only things that make these documents invalid מדרבנן. It does not list things that make them invalid מדאורייתא, like לשמה and מחובר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it teaches, it teaches invalidations from the רבנן. It does not teach those from the Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one answer that solves both questions: the ברייתא only lists rules set by the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document not written לשמה, or written while attached to the ground, is invalid by Torah law. The ברייתא was only listing invalidations made by the רבנן, so Torah-level rules were left out on purpose. This answers the question about לשמה even for רבא, and the question about מחובר for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: an invalidation set by the רבנן
from the Torah
it teaches

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's list of ways a גט and a שטר שחרור are alike is limited in two ways: it lists only rules special to these two documents (Step 8), and only rules from the רבנן, not from the Torah.

phrases.english: When it teaches, it teaches invalidation of the Rabbis;
invalidation from the Torah it does not teach.
phrases.notes: לשמה and מחובר are Torah-level rules, so they were left off the list.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי פְּסוּלָא דְרַבָּנַן, דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers both Step 11 (for רבא) and Step 13 (for both views) with one principle.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the list: it covers only invalidations from the רבנן.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list should include every invalidation shared by both documents, so לשמה and מחובר seem to be missing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list covers only invalidations from the רבנן. לשמה and מחובר come from the Torah, so they were left out on purpose.

steps.title: Gentile court documents seem invalid by Torah law, yet they are listed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 14. The ברייתא lists ערכאות של גוים, even though that seems to be a Torah-level disqualification.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא lists documents from gentile courts, and that is a disqualification from the Torah. So why is it listed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave, that the list contains only rabbinic rules. It points to one item on the list that looks like a Torah-level rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A document signed in a gentile court has signers who are not valid witnesses. If the signing witnesses are what make a גט work, then such a גט has no valid witnesses at all, and that is a Torah problem. So listing it breaks the rule from step 14 that only rabbinic disqualifications are listed.

keyTerms.meaning: Gentile courts, where documents are signed by non-Jewish officials
A disqualification that comes from the Torah
And yet it teaches it (it is listed)

phrases.english: But there is the case of gentile courts,
phrases.notes: This is one of the items listed in the ברייתא: a גט or שטר שחרור signed in a gentile court is invalid.

phrases.english: which is a disqualification from the Torah,
and yet it is taught in the list!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עַרְכָּאוֹת שֶׁל גּוֹיִם, דִּפְסוּלָא דְאוֹרָיְיתָא הוּא, וְקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14, which said that only rabbinic disqualifications are listed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא lists only rabbinic disqualifications
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ערכאות של גוים is on the list, yet it seems to be invalid מדאורייתא because the signers are not valid witnesses.

steps.title: The case has valid delivery witnesses, following רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the case is one where valid witnesses saw the document being handed over. It follows רבי אלעזר, who holds that the delivery witnesses are what make a גט work. So the gentile signatures cause only a rabbinic problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where there were valid witnesses to the handing over. This follows רבי אלעזר, who says that the witnesses to the handing over are what make the divorce work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 14. It explains why the gentile-court document is only a rabbinic problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי אלעזר, the witnesses who watch the גט being handed over are what make it work. The signers are not what counts. So if valid witnesses saw the handover, the גט works by Torah law, and the gentile signatures make it invalid only מדרבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: Witnesses who see the document being handed over
They 'cut', meaning they are what make the divorce take effect
The תנא who holds that the delivery witnesses make the גט work

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up עדי מסירה (witnesses to the handing over) with the witnesses who sign the document. In רבי אלעזר's view, only the handover witnesses matter by Torah law.

phrases.english: It is speaking where there were witnesses to the handing over,
and it follows רבי אלעזר, who says:
The witnesses to the handing over are what make the divorce work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 15 by setting the case where there were valid delivery witnesses.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the case and placing it in a specific opinion (רבי אלעזר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A gentile-court document has no valid witnesses, so it is invalid מדאורייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: With valid עדי מסירה, the גט works by Torah law according to רבי אלעזר. The gentile signatures make it invalid only מדרבנן.

steps.title: The משנה shows the תנא קמא does not hold like רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 16. In the משנה, רבי שמעון says gentile-court גיטין are valid, and רבי זירא explains that רבי שמעון follows רבי אלעזר. That implies the תנא קמא, who calls them invalid, does not follow רבי אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the end of the משנה says: רבי שמעון says even these are valid. And רבי זירא said that רבי שמעון went along with רבי אלעזר, who said the witnesses to the handing over are what make the divorce work. This shows that the תנא קמא does not hold that way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. It uses a משנה to show that whoever invalidates gentile-court גיטין is not following רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא says that following רבי אלעזר is exactly why רבי שמעון calls these גיטין valid. So the תנא קמא, who calls them invalid, must hold that the signing witnesses are what make the גט work. In his view, the gentile-court problem is Torah-level, and the answer of step 16 does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause or end part of a משנה or ברייתא
The תנא who says gentile-court גיטין and שטרי שחרור are valid
The אמורא who explains רבי שמעון's reasoning
By inference, from this it follows
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule that gentile-court גיטין are invalid comes from someone who does not hold like רבי אלעזר. That reopens the question of why a Torah-level disqualification is in the list.

phrases.english: But since it teaches in the latter clause,
phrases.notes: This is the end of the משנה on 10b, which says gentile-court documents are valid except for גיטין and שחרורי עבדים.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף אֵלּוּ כְּשֵׁירִין,
phrases.english: רבי שמעון says: Even these are valid,
and רבי זירא said:

phrases.aramaic: יָרַד רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְשִׁיטָתוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: רבי שמעון went along with the approach of רבי אלעזר,
who said that the witnesses to the handing over make the divorce work;
this implies that the first תנא does not hold that way!
phrases.notes: So the one who invalidates these גיטין is not following רבי אלעזר, which knocks down the answer of step 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִדְּקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אַף אֵלּוּ כְּשֵׁירִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 16 that the ברייתא follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that invalidating gentile-court גיטין follows רבי אלעזר and is therefore only rabbinic
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי זירא links רבי אלעזר's view to רבי שמעון, who calls these גיטין valid. So the תנא קמא, who invalidates them, holds that the signing witnesses make the גט work, and in his view the disqualification is מדאורייתא.
